claim: F-1 students are SSN-eligible only with on-campus employment (or for-service fellowship, OPT/CPT; all F-1 PhD students at Yale). "F-1 students who have secured on campus employment, are receiving for-service fellowships, or are working off-campus with OPT or CPT" qualify.
source: Yale OISS, New Students: SSN and ITIN
supports: Gate SSN application on having a Yale job offer
suggestedSimplification: International player can apply for SSN only after accepting an on-campus job

claim: SSA requires the job to exist or start soon: F-1 student must show 'a general on-campus job or has been offered one that will begin in the next 30 days, or an SSN will not be assigned'. Evidence: DSO letter + recent pay slip or original employer letter, OR an employer letter 'signed off' by the DSO; plus evidence of F-1 admission (I-94) and current I-20.
source: SSA POMS RM 10211.245 (eff. 02/07/2024) and SSA search-result summaries
supports: Document checklist: passport, I-94, I-20, OISS letter, employer letter
uncertainty: low (30-day phrasing from SSA search snippet; ssa.gov pages returned 403 to direct fetch)
suggestedSimplification: Require job offer starting within 30 days + OISS letter

claim: Yale route: submit SS-5 online, then take 'Online Control Number, passport, I-94 record, and your I-20' plus employer verification and an OISS letter (signed at OISS, 421 Temple St) to SSA at 150 Court Street, 4th Floor, New Haven 'within 45 calendar days'. Students may apply 'two weeks after registering with OISS'.
source: Yale OISS, How to Apply for an SSN; New Students: SSN and ITIN
supports: Multi-step SSN flow with a wait after OISS registration
suggestedSimplification: Two steps: OISS letter, then SSA office visit

claim: "The current time is 2-3 weeks, but we have heard of instances in which it takes in excess of 5-6 weeks to receive the card, especially during busy times of the year and holidays."
source: Yale OISS, How to Apply for an SSN
supports: Card arrives 2-3 weeks after SSA visit, sometimes 5-6
suggestedSimplification: SSN arrives 3 weeks after application

claim: Yale-specific statement on paying students before the SSN arrives: not found. Yale says students report the number later via Yale Hub 'Update SSN', which 'will feed electronically to Workday'. IRS lets employers file W-2 with 'Applied For' (paper) or all zeros (electronic) when an employee has applied but not received an SSN.
source: Yale OISS; Yale How to update SSN (July 2025); IRS Publication 15 (2026)
supports: Pay can plausibly start before SSN arrives; the SSN is attached later
uncertainty: high for Yale practice (not found); low for IRS rule
suggestedSimplification: Allow pay before SSN; record SSN when it arrives

topic: A1 Before starting work at Yale
claim: I-9 Section 1 'must be completed no later than the end of your first day of work'; candidates cannot begin work until background check is complete (staff guidance). Student hourly records are created 'on the Weekly pay schedule'.
source: Yale, Submitting Your I-9 Form; Yale Procedure 3600 PR.01 (rev. 2023-09-06)
supports: I-9 on day one; no SSN needed to start
uncertainty: medium (background-check rule is general staff guidance; may not apply to all student jobs)
suggestedSimplification: I-9 at 221 Whitney Ave I-9 Center before first shift

claim: IRS: you need an ITIN if you 'have a federal tax purpose and you're not eligible for an SSN', including a 'Nonresident alien student, professor or researcher filing a U.S. federal tax return'. Apply with Form W-7 attached to a tax return, via a Certifying Acceptance Agent, or in person. 'Allow 7 weeks... It can take 9-11 weeks if it's tax season (January 15 to April 30) or if you applied from overseas.'
source: IRS, Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (reviewed 2025-10-28)
supports: ITIN only for students without SSN eligibility; 7-week wait
suggestedSimplification: ITIN for non-working F-1 students with taxable scholarship; 7 weeks

claim: Yale: those 'receiving taxable scholarship or financial aid, but are not eligible for an SSN' may apply for an ITIN; requests go through OISS Connect; 'OISS cannot process ITIN applications for dependents (F-2 or J-2)'.
source: Yale OISS, New Students: SSN and ITIN
supports: ITIN path via OISS for non-workers with taxable stipend
suggestedSimplification: ITIN via OISS if no job but taxable stipend

claim: "International students and 17 year olds must open account at a Chase branch." Without an SSN bring "Current passport, proof of U.S. address and secondary identification (i.e. driver's license, state-issued ID, or Form I-20)." Chase: international students 'may not need a U.S. phone number or Social Security number (SSN)'.
source: Chase Secure Banking college offer; Chase, Opening a Bank Account as an International Student (2025-07-08)
supports: No SSN needed; branch only; passport + U.S. address proof + I-20
suggestedSimplification: Chase: branch, passport + I-20 + address; no SSN

claim: BofA does not require an SSN; international students 'Schedule an appointment to meet with an associate at a financial center'. Primary ID e.g. 'foreign passport with or without U.S. issued visa'; secondary e.g. foreign/U.S. driver's license, U.S. student ID; 'tax identification number (if applicable)' (FTIN, SSN or ITIN). Non-resident aliens give both foreign and U.S. address. Eligibility: 'You are not a U.S. citizen' and 'You have a physical address where you reside'.
source: Bank of America, How to Open a Bank Account as an International Student
supports: No SSN; in person; passport + secondary ID; foreign address too
suggestedSimplification: BofA: branch, passport + student ID; no SSN

claim: Online requires that you 'Know your Social Security Number (SSN) or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN)'. 'Non-U.S. citizens without a U.S. issued taxpayer identification number must provide a government issued ID that provides evidence of nationality or residence.' Nonresident aliens with a U.S. primary residence 'can apply in person by making an appointment at a Wells Fargo branch'. Primary IDs include passport and consular IDs (Mexico etc.).
source: Wells Fargo, What you'll need to open an Everyday Checking account; Open/close FAQs
supports: No SSN possible only in branch with passport; online needs SSN/ITIN
uncertainty: medium (FAQ also says branch applicants 'need to know your SSN or ITIN'; the non-TIN passport clause suggests branch exception)
suggestedSimplification: Wells Fargo: branch, passport, primary+secondary ID + address

claim: "To apply online, you must be a U.S. citizen or a U.S. resident alien and at least 18 years old", with U.S. physical address and SSN or ITIN. A Citi statement about nonresident aliens opening in branch: not found.
source: Citi (search-result text from citi.com banking pages; direct fetch of the eligibility block failed)
supports: F-1 nonresident cannot open Citi online
uncertainty: medium (quote from search snippet; branch policy for nonresidents not found)
suggestedSimplification: Citi: unavailable online to F-1 nonresidents; branch-only or unavailable

claim: "360 Checking is available to United States citizens or lawful permanent residents with a U.S. physical address ... who are at least 18 years old and have a U.S.-based mobile phone number with either a valid Social Security Number, or an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN)".
source: Capital One 360 Checking Account Disclosures (dated 5/20/2026)
supports: F-1 students (not citizens/LPRs) ineligible for 360 Checking
suggestedSimplification: Capital One: closed to F-1 students

claim: Workday: 'Click on the Pay Hub' -> 'Payment Elections' -> 'Add' account. 'It can take approximately one pay cycle for direct deposit to take effect. Until then, you may receive a paper check.' A payroll staff member 'must verbally confirm your direct deposit setup'. Only U.S. bank checking/savings accounts. 'The Payroll Department does not hold checks for pickup.' Processing 'cannot be expedited'.
source: Yale Payroll Toolkit, Direct Deposit
supports: Direct deposit change lags ~1 pay cycle; paper check meanwhile; needs U.S. account
uncertainty: low (another Yale page says 'one or two pay periods')
suggestedSimplification: Change takes effect after one weekly pay cycle; paper check in between

claim: Student employees: 'an employment record is created in the Student Employment supervisory organization on the Weekly pay schedule'; hourly students complete eTimesheets weekly; supervisors approve 'by 3:00pm each Monday'.
source: Yale Procedure 3600 PR.01 Student Employment Procedures (rev. 2023-09-06)
supports: Weekly student pay; Monday approval cutoff
suggestedSimplification: Weekly pay; hours approved Monday

claim: Federal: 'not more than 20 hours per week while school is in session'; full-time during holiday/vacation. Yale policy: students 'may not work more than 19 hours (combined for all jobs) in any week during the academic terms'; PhD students 'always subject to the 20 hours per week limitation'. New students may work 'up to, but no more, than 30 days prior to the commencement of classes'.
source: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(9)(i); Yale OISS F-1 On-Campus Employment
supports: 19h/week cap in term at Yale; full-time in breaks (non-PhD)
suggestedSimplification: Cap 19h/week in term, 40h in breaks

claim: On-campus employment authorization 'shall be terminated upon completion or termination of the student's course of study'. Requires being 'enrolled in a full course of study'.
source: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(9)(i) via Cornell LII; Yale OISS
supports: Job authorization ends at graduation, dismissal or withdrawal
suggestedSimplification: End all on-campus jobs on completion/dismissal/withdrawal

claim: On-campus = work 'on the premises of Yale University or for which you receive a Yale paycheck'; commercial firms on campus providing 'direct services to Yale students' (prior OISS approval); off-campus with 'official educational relationship' (prior approval). Whether the Yale Summer Cabaret counts: not found. Summer Cabaret is described as 'student-run' and the 'exploratory theatrical home for David Geffen School of Drama students'; payment/payroll status not found.
source: Yale OISS F-1 On-Campus Employment; Yale/DGSD search results
supports: Cabaret counts only if paid via Yale payroll or approved by OISS
suggestedSimplification: Treat Cabaret pay as on-campus only if paid through Yale payroll; otherwise unauthorized for F-1

claim: "An F-1 student who has completed a course of study and any authorized practical training following completion of studies will be allowed an additional 60-day period to prepare for departure from the United States or to transfer... An F-1 student authorized by the DSO to withdraw from classes will be allowed a 15-day period for departure from the United States. However, an F-1 student who fails to maintain a full course of study without the approval of the DSO or otherwise fails to maintain status is not eligible for an additional period for departure."
source: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(iv), 2025 CFR edition (GovInfo)
supports: 60 days after graduation; 15 after authorized withdrawal; 0 after dismissal/status failure
suggestedSimplification: Graduate: 60 days; withdraw: 15; dismissed: 0

topic: B6 Duration of status final rule (enjoined)
claim: DHS final rule eliminating D/S was published July 17, 2026 (91 FR 44976), effective Sept 15, 2026; it would cut the post-completion grace period to 30 days and renumber it to (f)(5)(v). On Sept 14, 2026 the D. Mass. court (Presidents' Alliance et al. v. DHS) 'issued an order preliminarily enjoining DHS from implementing this rule'. Yale: 'the current D/S framework remains in place for now'; 'the rule may still take effect later'. Cornell LII already shows the amended 30-day text.
source: Yale OISS, Elimination of Duration of Status FAQs; AILA featured issue
supports: Live legal uncertainty for fall 2026 game
suggestedSimplification: Use 60-day rule; optionally note it may become 30

claim: OPT specifics not researched in this pass beyond: SSN eligibility includes OPT; on-campus authorization ends at completion. Not found / not verified here.
source: n/a
suggestedSimplification: Leave OPT out or treat as a separate application

claim: IRC 3121(b)(10) excludes 'service performed in the employ of a school, college, or university' by 'a student who is enrolled and regularly attending classes'. Rev. Proc. 2005-11: half-time graduate students qualify; no exception for 'school breaks of more than five weeks (including summer breaks of more than five weeks)' if not enrolled.
source: 26 USC 3121 (Cornell LII); IRS Student exception to FICA tax (reviewed 2026-10-09); Rev. Proc. 2005-11
supports: Term-time Yale wages exempt from FICA for enrolled students
suggestedSimplification: No FICA on term-time Yale wages

claim: Yale: payments for services by a student 'enrolled at the university at least half time during an academic term are generally exempt from FICA tax'; 'Other Wages (Summer)' are subject to FICA at 7.65% (6.2% + 1.45%).
source: Yale, Tax Treatment of Certain Payments ... U.S. Citizens and Resident Aliens
supports: US-citizen player: summer Yale wages pay 7.65% FICA; term wages don't
suggestedSimplification: Citizen: FICA 7.65% in summer only

claim: IRC 3121(b)(19) excludes service 'performed by a nonresident alien individual for the period he is temporarily present in the United States as a nonimmigrant under subparagraph (F), (J), (M), or (Q)' for the visa's purpose. IRS: F-1 nonresidents (generally first 5 calendar years) are 'exempt from Social Security Tax and Medicare Tax' on on-campus, authorized off-campus and practical-training wages.
source: 26 USC 3121 (Cornell LII); IRS Foreign student liability for Social Security and Medicare taxes (reviewed 2026-08-18)
supports: International player: no FICA year-round including summer
suggestedSimplification: F-1: never FICA during the game's span

claim: Federal withholding on W-2 wages per Form W-4; Connecticut withholding per Form CT-W4. Nonresident alien fellowships withheld at 14% (F/J/M/Q) and reported on Form 1042-S; treaty exemption on wages needs Form 8233, effective 'payments made 10 days from the date the University Tax Department mails the original Form 8233 to the IRS'.
source: Yale tax pages; Yale Tax Reporting & Withholding
supports: Withholding on wages always; 14% on F-1 non-service stipend
suggestedSimplification: Wages: fed + CT withholding; F-1 stipend: 14%

claim: US-UK Art. 20: student payments exempt only if they 'arise outside' the U.S. and are for maintenance, education or training. US-Mexico Art. 21: exempt 'amounts received from sources outside the United States' for maintenance, education or training. Neither exempts Yale (U.S.-source) wages for students; a specific student-wages exemption for either: not found.
source: Treasury / IRS treaty texts and technical explanations (search-result text)
supports: No treaty relief on Yale wages for Mexican or UK players
uncertainty: medium (verbatim treaty text not fetched; UK text https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/131/Treaty-UK-7-24-2001.pdf)
suggestedSimplification: No treaty break for Mexico/UK on Yale pay

claim: Nonresidents file Form 1040-NR. Due 'April 15' if you received wages subject to withholding; 'June 15' if no wages subject to withholding and no U.S. office.
source: IRS, Taxation of Nonresident Aliens (updated 2026-02-17)
supports: Working F-1: April 15; stipend-only F-1: June 15
suggestedSimplification: Working players file by April 15

claim: Form 8843 explains exclusion of days from the substantial presence test for exempt individuals (F students). 'If you don't have to file a 2025 tax return, mail Form 8843 ... by the due date (including extensions) for filing Form 1040-NR' (Austin, TX 73301-0215).
supports: Every F-1 player files 8843 even with no income
suggestedSimplification: F-1: 8843 every spring, attached to 1040-NR or alone by June 15

claim: Tax-free if a degree candidate and used for 'tuition and fees required for enrollment or attendance' and required 'fees, books, supplies, and equipment'; taxable: 'room and board, travel', and pay 'for teaching, research, or other services required as a condition'. Yale: graduate stipends taxable though not reported on W-2/1099 for citizens; 'does NOT relieve the recipient from the obligation of reporting'.
source: IRS Topic 421 (reviewed 2026-09-24); Yale tax page
supports: Tuition scholarship untaxed; living stipend taxed
suggestedSimplification: Tax only the living-stipend part

claim: 7 CFR 273.5(a): 'An individual who is enrolled at least half-time in an institution of higher education shall be ineligible to participate in SNAP unless' exempt. Exemptions include (b)(5) 'employed for a minimum of 20 hours per week and be paid' and (b)(6) 'participating in a State or federally financed work study program during the regular school year'. CT: 20 hours averaged monthly, at least 80 hours/month (CT DSS).
source: 7 CFR 273.5 (Cornell LII); CT DSS Students / Eligible Student Criteria
supports: Grad student ineligible unless 20+ paid hours or work-study
uncertainty: low (CT 80-hour detail from search snippet; DSS page rejected fetch)
suggestedSimplification: Yale's 19h cap means Yale job alone can't satisfy 20h; only work-study or outside job

claim: After OBBB (enacted July 4, 2025) 'the only aliens eligible for SNAP are those with the following statuses: lawful permanent resident (LPR), Cuban and Haitian entrant (CHE), or Compacts of Free Association (COFA) citizen'. CT applied this from November 2025. F-1 students are none of these.
source: USDA FNS OBBB alien eligibility memo; CT DSS H.R.1 Non-citizen eligibility
supports: F-1 player never SNAP-eligible
suggestedSimplification: SNAP closed to F-1 players

claim: CGS 31-222 (subdivision (5)(G) of the employment definition) excludes 'Service performed in the employ of a school, college, or university if such service is performed (i) by a student who is enrolled and is regularly attending classes at such school, college or university'. Federal parallel FUTA 3306(c)(10)(B).
source: CGS ch. 567 (cga.ct.gov, current); 26 USC 3306 (Cornell LII)
supports: Yale student-job wages earn no UI wage credits
uncertainty: low (exact paragraph label inferred: '(5) No provision of this chapter ... shall apply to ... (G)')
suggestedSimplification: Yale student wages never count toward unemployment

topic: C10 CT UI students & after graduation
claim: CGS 31-235(a)(2): not unavailable 'solely because the individual is attending a school ... as a regularly enrolled student', but 31-235(b) bars this for a claimant who was a full-time student in the prior two years 'unless such claimant was employed on a full-time basis ... for the two years'. 31-236(a)(6): ineligible if 'left employment to attend a school ... during such attendance'. CT DOL: 'You must be willing to change classes or drop out of school if a job conflicts with your courses.' Post-graduation claim based only on excluded Yale student wages: no qualifying wages, so no benefits (inferred; explicit statement not found).
source: CGS 31-235, 31-236; CT DOL knowledge base (2021-11-24)
supports: Students effectively ineligible; grad with only student wages has no base
suggestedSimplification: No UI for the player from Yale student work

claim: FUTA 3304(a)(14)(A): benefits not payable on services by an alien unless the alien 'was lawfully admitted for permanent residence ... was lawfully present for purposes of performing such services, or was permanently residing in the United States under color of law'. Availability for work also requires work authorization (CT-specific F-1 statement not found).
source: 26 USC 3304 (Cornell LII)
supports: F-1 player after status ends cannot claim
suggestedSimplification: F-1: no UI

claim: CGS 31-275(9) 'Employee' means any person who '(i) Has entered into or works under any contract of service or apprenticeship with an employer'. The exclusions list (casual employment, family members, domestic work, etc.) contains no student exclusion; 'student' appears only in dependency definitions. Yale: injured employees report to supervisor; TPA CorVel (833-400-7222); first report 'within 24 hours'.
source: CGS ch. 568 (cga.ct.gov); Yale OGC Reporting Accidents/Insurance Claims
supports: Student employees covered as employees
uncertainty: low-medium (no explicit 'students are covered' sentence found; inferred from absence of exclusion)
suggestedSimplification: Injured on a Yale job = workers' comp

claim: CGS 31-307(a): weekly compensation 'equal to seventy-five per cent of the injured employee's average weekly earnings ... after such earnings have been reduced by any deduction for federal or state taxes, or both, and for the federal Insurance Contributions Act'; capped at the 31-309 maximum; minimum 20% of the maximum but not above 75% of AWW. Max for injuries on/after Oct 1, 2026: $1,776.00 (total).
source: CGS 31-307; CT WCC Memorandum 2026-05 (2026-09-04)
supports: TTD = 75% of after-tax AWW
suggestedSimplification: 75% of after-tax weekly wage; floor min(20% x $1,776, 75% AWW)

claim: CGS 31-295(a): no compensation for an injury that does not incapacitate 'for a period of more than three days'; if more than three but less than seven days, compensation 'shall begin at the expiration of the first three days'; 'If the incapacity continues for a period of seven days, compensation shall begin from the date of the injury.' (b) Full wages for the day of injury.
supports: 3-day wait, retroactive at 7 days
suggestedSimplification: Pay from day 4; from day 1 if out 7+ days

claim: CGS 31-294d(a)(1): employer 'shall provide a competent physician ... and, in addition, shall furnish any medical and surgical aid or hospital and nursing service, including medical rehabilitation services and prescription drugs' as deemed reasonable or necessary.
source: CGS 31-294d
supports: Employer pays all work-injury medical costs, no wait
suggestedSimplification: Work-injury medical bills fully covered

claim: CT, effective Oct 1, 2026, HUSKY eligibility for non-citizens limited to LPRs with 5+ years, Cuban/Haitian entrants and COFA citizens. 'HUSKY LB – Emergency Medicaid' covers certain emergency services for residents meeting all requirements 'except immigration status'. F-1 students: not eligible for full HUSKY (inferred).
source: CT DSS H.R.1 Non-citizen eligibility; CT DSS search results
supports: F-1: emergency Medicaid only
suggestedSimplification: F-1: no HUSKY except emergencies

claim: Marketplace requires citizenship/nationality or lawful presence; 'Valid non-immigrant visas' are lawfully present. From Jan 1, 2027 only LPRs, Cuban/Haitian entrants and COFA migrants qualify for premium tax credits / CSRs. After F-1 status ends (no lawful presence): not eligible (inferred).
source: HealthCare.gov, Health coverage for lawfully present immigrants
supports: F-1 can buy unsubsidized plans; no subsidy from 2027; none after status ends
uncertainty: medium (2026 sub-100% FPL change not verified)
suggestedSimplification: F-1: Marketplace at full price only; Yale Health is the realistic coverage
